purpose: Machine-facing applied knowledge base for finding, grading, and synthesizing authoritative motivation and decision-psychology work-units (motivation theory, self-regulation, heuristics/biases, emotion) for productivity, decision, and behavior-design support; strictly informational and applied, not clinical diagnosis or mental-health treatment, which are flagged for professional referral.
assumptions: No observed dataset or experimental evidence supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.
This unit is a subdomain node of Applied Psychology within a knowledge-searcher meta-KB.
Nodes are concrete, evaluable work-units/methods/decision areas, not abstract topics.
Canonical works (Kahneman 'Thinking, Fast and Slow'; Pink 'Drive'; Deci & Ryan SDT) inform priors but are weighted by replication status.
exclusions: Psychotherapy, treatment planning, or medication guidance.
Crisis counseling or intervention (routed to professional referral).
Non-applied pure theory with no work-unit translation.

glossary.definition: motivation arising from inherent interest or enjoyment of a task
tendency to weigh losses more heavily than equivalent gains relative to a reference point
an if-then plan linking a situational cue to a goal-directed response
overweighting immediate outcomes relative to future ones in intertemporal choice
using current feelings as information when judging risk or value
reinterpreting a situation's meaning to change its emotional impact
design of how options are presented to influence decisions without removing options
a rating of a claim's strength from replication, effect size, and generalizability
reduction of intrinsic motivation caused by adding controlling extrinsic rewards
request content indicating diagnosis, treatment, or crisis needs requiring referral

evidence_label_policy.rationale: no observed dataset or experimental evidence supplied; all estimates reference SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR

source_registry.description: Model heuristic priors over applied motivation and decision psychology, informed by canonical works (Kahneman 'Thinking, Fast and Slow'; Pink 'Drive'; Deci & Ryan SDT) without supplied datasets.

nodes.definition: Bound the unit to informational, applied motivation/decision work-units and exclude clinical diagnosis or treatment.

included: informational explanation of drives and choices

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: request pattern shifts toward symptom or treatment language

pros.claim: Prevents harmful overreach into clinical advice
pros.example: route 'I think I'm depressed, what meds' to professional referral

pros.claim: Stabilizes what counts as a valid work-unit
pros.example: accept 'reduce procrastination on reports', reject 'diagnose my ADHD'

cons.claim: Hard boundary cases blur applied vs clinical
cons.example: 'chronic low motivation' may be subclinical or clinical

cons.claim: Over-restriction can refuse benign applied requests
cons.example: declining all stress questions is too broad

failure_modes: clinical request answered as applied advice
acceptance_tests: every output classifies request as in-scope or referral

nodes.definition: Define and operationalize each motivation/decision construct so retrieval and synthesis target the right phenomenon.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: construct found to conflate two distinct phenomena

pros.example: separate 'intrinsic motivation' from 'flow'

pros.claim: Anchors search terms to measurable phenomena
pros.example: map willpower to ego-depletion/self-control measures

cons.claim: Operational choices can bias which evidence is found
cons.example: defining motivation only via behavior misses self-report

acceptance_tests: each construct has one operational definition

nodes.definition: Model autonomy, competence, and relatedness needs and how they drive intrinsic vs extrinsic motivation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: autonomy-support intervention fails to raise persistence

pros.example: contingent rewards crowd out intrinsic interest
give choice + rationale to raise autonomy

cons.claim: Hard to isolate need satisfaction empirically

acceptance_tests: recommendations map to a named need
crowding-out risk checked when adding incentives
revisit_triggers: incentive added to a task design

nodes.definition: Apply specific, difficult, committed goals with feedback to direct and energize effort.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: specific-hard goals reduce performance via tunnel vision

pros.claim: Robust effect of specific hard goals on output
pros.example: 'finish 3 sections by Friday' beats 'do your best'
weekly progress review sustains effort

cons.claim: Goals can induce gaming or tunnel vision

nodes.definition: Predict motivation from expectancy of success times subjective value minus cost (expectancy-value/instrumentality).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: value high but behavior absent, implicating cost not expectancy

pros.example: raise expectancy via scaffolding
high effort cost suppresses a valued task

cons.claim: Subjective value is hard to elicit

acceptance_tests: estimate names expectancy, value, and cost

nodes.definition: Model self-control, willpower allocation, and delay of gratification as regulation of impulses toward goals.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: ego-depletion replication evidence updates willpower-as-resource view

pros.claim: Targets the proximal cause of procrastination
pros.example: precommit to remove temptation
situational restructuring beats raw effort

acceptance_tests: claims about depletion cite replication status

nodes.definition: Convert goals into if-then plans that automate cue-triggered action and close the intention-action gap.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: effect size shrinks in field vs lab settings

pros.example: 'if it's 9am, then I draft for 25 min'
'if tempted by phone, then put it in another room'

cons.claim: Effects can be modest and decay

failure_modes: plan never linked to a real cue
acceptance_tests: each plan has concrete cue and response

nodes.definition: Diagnose procrastination as emotion-regulation-driven delay and design counter-mechanisms.
contradictors: view treating it purely as time-management

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: emotion-regulation framing outperforms time-management framing

pros.claim: Reframes delay as mood repair, not laziness
pros.example: address task aversion not just scheduling
add near-term subgoals and deadlines

nodes.definition: Frame judgment as fast automatic System 1 and slow deliberate System 2 to locate where errors arise.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: dual-process dichotomy challenged by continuous-evidence models

pros.claim: Locates whether to debias or redesign cue
pros.example: slow down with checklist vs change default
biases mapped to System 1 shortcuts

acceptance_tests: attribution justified by cue, not outcome

nodes.definition: Catalog systematic judgment biases (anchoring, availability, representativeness) and their decision impact.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: ecological-rationality evidence reframes a 'bias' as adaptive

pros.example: anchoring distorts numeric estimates
consider-the-opposite for overconfidence

acceptance_tests: each bias tied to a concrete decision feature
revisit_triggers: replication failure for a cited bias

nodes.definition: Model choice under risk via reference-dependence, loss aversion, and probability weighting.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: loss-aversion coefficient varies more than canonical 2:1

pros.claim: Explains risk attitude flips around reference
pros.example: risk-seeking in losses, averse in gains

pros.claim: Reference framing is an actionable lever
pros.example: frame retirement as protecting a gain

cons.claim: Loss-aversion magnitude is overstated at times

cons.example: status quo vs aspiration as reference

nodes.definition: Use framing, defaults, and choice architecture to shape decisions without changing options.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: nudge effect fails to replicate at scale or erodes trust

pros.claim: Defaults move behavior at low cost
pros.example: opt-out enrollment lifts participation

pros.claim: Framing aligns choice with stated goals
pros.example: emphasize gains to encourage uptake

cons.example: dark patterns exploit the same levers

cons.claim: Nudges can backfire or erode trust

acceptance_tests: ethics note attached to each nudge

nodes.definition: Model how future outcomes are discounted and how present bias drives intertemporal choice.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: hyperbolic vs quasi-hyperbolic fit differs for the population

pros.claim: Explains why distant goals lose to now
pros.example: gym tomorrow loses to couch today
auto-transfer to savings on payday

failure_modes: assuming a single stable discount rate

nodes.definition: Account for how affect, mood, and the affect heuristic bias motivation and decisions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: incidental affect found to dominate integral affect in context

pros.claim: Explains fast risk judgments via feeling
pros.example: dread inflates perceived risk
unrelated bad mood taxes a choice

cons.claim: Affect is hard to measure in the moment

acceptance_tests: assessment separates incidental vs integral affect

nodes.definition: Apply reappraisal, distancing, and situation selection to regulate affect supporting goals (non-clinical).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: reappraisal less effective under high stress than expected

pros.example: reframe a setback as a challenge
avoid the trigger environment

cons.claim: Risk of crossing into clinical territory
Reappraisal can fail under acute stress

nodes.definition: Grade strength of psychological evidence accounting for replication, effect size, and generalizability.
contradictors: author citing single famous study uncritically

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a relied-upon finding fails a registered replication

pros.example: downweight ego-depletion classic effect
lab undergrads not the whole population

cons.example: perfect evidence is rare in psychology

acceptance_tests: each major claim has an evidence grade
replication status checked for cited effects
revisit_triggers: claim used outside its sample population

nodes.definition: Locate and select authoritative motivation/decision sources (seminal books, meta-analyses, reviews).
contradictors: user wanting only viral pop summaries

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: key meta-analysis supersedes prior primary studies

pros.example: prefer a meta-analysis to one anchoring study
spot missing cross-cultural evidence

cons.example: Thinking Fast and Slow predates some replication updates

nodes.definition: Translate motivation/decision findings into concrete productivity, behavior-design, and decision-support recommendations.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: intervention fails its measurement plan in the field

pros.example: combine if-then plans + default to cut procrastination
define a metric before deploying

cons.claim: Effect transfer to context is uncertain
cons.example: lab effect may not survive deployment

nodes.definition: Detect and control the searcher's own biases (confirmation, anchoring on first source) during synthesis.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: audit repeatedly finds one-sided syntheses

pros.example: force a search for disconfirming evidence

pros.claim: Counters anchoring on the first source read
pros.example: weight later sources equally

cons.example: not all sides are equally supported

acceptance_tests: no claim rests on a single anchor source

nodes.definition: Detect clinical or crisis signals in requests and escalate to professional referral instead of advising.
contradictors: user demanding the system act as a therapist

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new clinical-signal pattern or crisis-language class observed

pros.claim: Prevents harm from out-of-scope clinical advice
pros.example: route self-harm language to crisis resources
explicitly hand off rather than advise

acceptance_tests: clinical/crisis phrases trigger referral not advice

edges.why_related: Scope decisions gate which constructs are even in play.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Construct work stays inside applied scope.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Defining clinical constructs leaks out of scope.
edges.example: scope excludes 'major depressive disorder' before construct list is built
edges.resolution_rule: SCOPE_BOUNDARY dominates; out-of-scope constructs dropped

edges.why_related: Scope boundary defines what counts as a clinical signal to escalate.
edges.example: scope marks self-harm language clinical -> escalation triggers
edges.resolution_rule: scope definition is source of truth for escalation triggers

edges.why_related: SDT needs precise need-construct definitions.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Avoids conflating autonomy with mere choice.
edges.example: define autonomy operationally before recommending autonomy support
edges.resolution_rule: construct definitions precede theory application

edges.why_related: Goal-setting needs operational goal/commitment constructs.
edges.example: operationalize 'commitment' before measuring it
edges.resolution_rule: construct layer precedes goal-setting

edges.why_related: Bias catalog needs each bias operationally defined.
edges.example: separate anchoring from availability before cataloging
edges.resolution_rule: define-before-catalog

edges.why_related: Grading needs to know which construct a study measured.
edges.example: grade evidence for 'grit' only against grit measures
edges.resolution_rule: construct mapping precedes grading

edges.why_related: Retrieval queries are built from defined constructs.
edges.example: search terms derived from construct glossary
edges.resolution_rule: glossary feeds query design

edges.why_related: Process attribution changes which biases are expected.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Biases mapped to the implicated process.
edges.example: System 1 attribution surfaces anchoring/availability
edges.resolution_rule: attribution must match cue evidence, not outcome

edges.why_related: Dual-process framing uses defined cognition constructs.
edges.example: define deliberation before labeling System 2
edges.resolution_rule: constructs precede process framing

edges.why_related: Prospect-theory analysis builds on the bias inventory.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Risk effects grounded in known biases.
edges.example: loss aversion examined after listing relevant biases
edges.resolution_rule: run bias inventory before risk modeling

edges.why_related: Reference-dependence and loss aversion power framing levers.
edges.example: loss-averse frame ('don't lose your gains') drives a default
edges.resolution_rule: set reference point before designing the frame

edges.why_related: Both model deviations from rational choice under risk/time.
edges.example: risk and time preferences both nonlinear
edges.resolution_rule: keep as distinct mechanisms; do not merge

edges.why_related: Framing/choice-architecture findings become applied specs.
edges.example: default-enrollment spec for a productivity tool
edges.resolution_rule: applied spec must carry ethics + evidence checks

edges.why_related: Need-support recommendations feed applied interventions.
edges.example: design a task with choice + rationale
edges.resolution_rule: check crowding-out before adding rewards

edges.why_related: If-then plans operationalize an already-specified goal.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Plans without a real goal misfire.
edges.example: goal '3 sections by Fri' -> 'if 9am then draft'
edges.resolution_rule: specify goal before forming if-then plans

edges.why_related: Self-control mechanisms explain and counter procrastination.
edges.example: situational restructuring reduces task aversion
edges.resolution_rule: address regulation/aversion before scheduling

edges.why_related: Present bias is a key input to self-control failures.
edges.example: precommitment counters discount-driven lapse
edges.resolution_rule: model discounting when designing self-control

edges.why_related: If-then plans are a direct procrastination counter-mechanism.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Vague cues fail to start the task.
edges.example: 'if I open the laptop then I write one line'
edges.resolution_rule: ensure cue is concrete and obstacle-aware

edges.why_related: Regulation needs an affect assessment to target.
edges.example: incidental mood identified before reappraisal
edges.resolution_rule: assess affect before choosing a regulation strategy

edges.why_related: The affect heuristic is itself a judgment shortcut.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Double-counting affect as a separate bias.
edges.example: dread inflates risk via the affect heuristic
edges.resolution_rule: represent affect heuristic once, cross-reference

edges.why_related: Regulation attempts can reveal clinical-severity signals that trigger escalation.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Continuing applied advice on clinical distress.
edges.example: reappraisal fails + distress persists -> referral
edges.resolution_rule: stop condition: escalate after repeated ineffective regulation or severity cue

edges.why_related: Persistent paralysis can signal clinical avoidance needing referral.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Pushing applied fixes on a clinical case.
edges.example: months of paralysis despite plans -> referral
edges.resolution_rule: stop condition: escalate when applied mechanisms repeatedly fail

edges.why_related: Only graded findings should be translated to interventions.
edges.example: downgraded ego-depletion finding excluded from a spec
edges.resolution_rule: grading gates translation

edges.why_related: Grading gaps trigger more retrieval of better sources.
edges.example: low grade -> fetch a meta-analysis
edges.resolution_rule: stop condition: stop when grade threshold met or budget reached

edges.why_related: Known biases inform the searcher's own self-audit.
edges.example: anchoring knowledge -> check first-source anchoring
edges.resolution_rule: map self-audit to catalogued biases

edges.why_related: Bias audit weighs claims by their evidence grades.
edges.example: strong-grade claim not 'balanced' against a weak one
edges.resolution_rule: use grades to weight, not to force symmetry

edges.why_related: Bias audit constrains which synthesis may be operationalized.
edges.example: spec blocked until counter-evidence search done
edges.resolution_rule: no translation until bias audit passes

edges.why_related: Sources are retrieved before they can be graded.
edges.example: retrieve meta-analyses, then grade them
edges.resolution_rule: retrieve-then-grade ordering

edges.why_related: Expectancy-value decomposition guides which lever an intervention pulls.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Pulling the wrong term (value vs cost).
edges.example: reduce effort cost in a productivity redesign
edges.resolution_rule: target weakest of expectancy/value/cost

edges.why_related: Imposed hard goals can undercut autonomy and intrinsic motivation.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Externally set quotas crush intrinsic interest.
edges.example: assigned stretch quota lowers autonomy
edges.resolution_rule: prefer participatively-set goals; if imposed, add autonomy support

edges.why_related: Nudges/defaults can reduce experienced autonomy.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Manipulative defaults harm autonomy and trust.
edges.example: forced default triggers reactance
edges.resolution_rule: preserve transparency + easy opt-out; autonomy dominates on ethics

edges.why_related: Pressure to ship interventions conflicts with strict evidence gating.
edges.example: deadline pushes to ship an ungraded nudge
edges.resolution_rule: evidence grading dominates; rigor over speed

edges.why_related: Persuasive framing must yield to referral when distress is clinical.
edges.example: stop nudging, route to referral on crisis signal
edges.resolution_rule: escalation dominates framing on any clinical signal

edges.why_related: Discounting estimates shape precommitment interventions.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Ignoring present bias in the spec.
edges.example: auto-save precommitment in a finance app
edges.resolution_rule: include precommitment for present-biased targets

edges.why_related: Whether to nudge System 1 or prompt System 2 depends on process attribution.
edges.example: complex choice -> add deliberation step not a nudge
edges.resolution_rule: match intervention to implicated process

edges.why_related: Both explain motivation but via needs vs expectancy/value.
edges.example: autonomy need vs expectancy as competing accounts
edges.resolution_rule: keep distinct; triangulate, do not merge

edges.why_related: Evidence limits constrain how confidently applied claims near clinical lines are made.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Overconfident advice on weak evidence near clinical scope.
edges.example: weak evidence near clinical line -> caution/referral
edges.resolution_rule: low grade near clinical scope biases toward referral

conflict_axes.trigger: an imposed goal, incentive, or default is added to a motivation design
resolution_order: add autonomy support if control needed
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: On ethics and long-run intrinsic motivation, autonomy support dominates; short-term compliance levers allowed only with autonomy support and opt-out.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: control mechanism removes informed choice or targets a vulnerable user
conflict_axes.example: assigned stretch quota vs participatively-set goal with rationale

conflict_axes.trigger: a nudge/default/frame could move behavior against the user's reflective interest
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Informed-choice preservation dominates persuasion effectiveness; dark patterns forbidden.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: frame exploits a clinical or crisis state
conflict_axes.example: opt-out default that is hard to reverse vs transparent opt-out

conflict_axes.trigger: deadline pressure to ship an intervention before evidence is graded
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Evidence grading dominates speed; ungraded findings may not be operationalized.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: ungraded claim would drive an irreversible decision
conflict_axes.example: shipping an ungraded nudge under deadline

conflict_axes.trigger: adding extrinsic rewards to an intrinsically motivated task
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Protect existing intrinsic motivation; use rewards informationally when interest is low.
conflict_axes.example: paying for a hobby task that was already enjoyed

conflict_axes.trigger: a request mixes applied productivity needs with clinical-severity distress
resolution_order: offer applied help only for in-scope remainder
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Clinical escalation dominates applied advice whenever any clinical/crisis signal is present.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: any self-harm, crisis, or diagnosis-seeking signal
conflict_axes.example: 'I can't get out of bed and want to disappear' -> referral, not productivity tips

conflict_axes.trigger: a present temptation competes with a committed future goal
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Use precommitment and near-term structure so the future goal is protected without relying on raw willpower.
conflict_axes.example: scrolling now vs writing the report due next week

conflict_axes.trigger: a famous seminal claim conflicts with newer replication evidence
resolution_order: cite seminal work as origin not proof
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Current replication-weighted evidence dominates seminal status when they conflict.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a core recommendation rests on a failed-replication classic
conflict_axes.example: ego-depletion in a famous book vs failed replications

conflict_axes.trigger: debiasing pressure pushes toward false balance between unequal evidence
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Grade-weighting dominates; balance means proportional representation, not equal weight.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a weak claim is elevated to parity with strong evidence
conflict_axes.example: 'both sides' framing of a well-replicated vs fringe finding

edge_cases.trigger: a clinical/crisis request is handled as applied advice
edge_cases.example: answering 'what antidepressant should I take' with applied tips
edge_cases.detection_method: clinical/crisis phrase classifier flags request before any advice is emitted

edge_cases.trigger: a failed-replication classic is cited as solid
edge_cases.detection_method: replication-status check against grading registry per cited effect

edge_cases.trigger: two constructs are treated as one
edge_cases.example: using flow research to support intrinsic-motivation claims

edge_cases.detection_method: ethics checklist requires transparency + easy reversal per nudge

edge_cases.example: only citing studies that support a favored theory
edge_cases.detection_method: require a logged disconfirming-evidence search before synthesis lock

edge_cases.trigger: a node tries to cover all biases plus theory
edge_cases.failure_mode: node too large for one session/handoff
edge_cases.example: merging dual-process and the whole bias catalog
edge_cases.detection_method: node grain check: inputs/outputs exceed single-session scope

edge_cases.trigger: a computed score is edited without recomputation
edge_cases.example: final_importance hand-edited away from formula value
edge_cases.detection_method: validator recomputes all derived fields within tolerance 0.02

edge_cases.trigger: an edge or dependency points to a removed node
edge_cases.example: edge to a renamed node id
edge_cases.detection_method: reference validator checks every from/to/dependency against node ids

edge_cases.example: A depends on B depends on A via mislabeled edges
edge_cases.detection_method: DFS cycle detection over dependency edges + node.dependencies

edge_cases.trigger: a value is labeled observed without a dataset
edge_cases.detection_method: label scan rejects observed/experimentally_validated without data

edge_cases.trigger: a high-risk artifact is hard-locked before review
edge_cases.example: locking a clinical-escalation rule without human review
edge_cases.detection_method: lock-state check: hard_lock requires passed gates + human review

high coupling; feeds every theory/evidence node
central bias catalog used by many nodes

dominance_rules.trigger: any clinical or crisis signal present
dominance_rules.rule: Clinical escalation dominates all applied advice.
dominance_rules.required_action: route to professional referral and stop applied output

dominance_rules.example: deadline cannot ship an ungraded nudge

dominance_rules.trigger: dependency order conflicts with value order
dominance_rules.required_action: finalize prerequisites before high-value downstream nodes
dominance_rules.example: grade before translating even if translation is valued

dominance_rules.rule: Informed-choice and safety dominate persuasion power.
dominance_rules.required_action: attach ethics note; forbid dark patterns

dominance_rules.trigger: numeric precision vs evidence label legality
dominance_rules.rule: Correct evidence labels dominate numeric precision.

dominance_rules.trigger: human review vs automation on high-risk nodes
dominance_rules.rule: Human review dominates automation for high-risk/irreversible nodes.

dominance_rules.trigger: schema stability vs adding more content
dominance_rules.example: do not add clinical nodes to inflate density

dominance_rules.required_action: cite seminal as origin, weight by replication
dominance_rules.example: prefer meta-analysis over a classic book claim

anti_rework_rules.rule: Lock scope and escalation before any construct or content work.
Define constructs before retrieving or grading evidence.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: avoids grading the wrong construct's studies

anti_rework_rules.rule: Grade evidence before translating to interventions.
Run the bias audit before locking a synthesis.
Specify goals before forming implementation intentions.

anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: plan exists with no parent goal

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attribute the process before selecting bias or nudge interventions.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Compute all derived scores from formulas, never hand-edit.
Check crowding-out before adding extrinsic incentives.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pass validation and human review before any hard lock.
